payload.name: Split Multi-Claim Messages During Extraction
payload.description: Use during extraction when a message contains both a factual event and an explicit subjective reaction, feeling, or evaluation about it; create separate durable candidates instead of one merged summary.
content: During extraction, when one message states multiple distinct durable claims—such as a narrated event plus the speaker's explicit subjective reaction or feeling about it—create one candidate per claim; do not merge them into a single event summary.
Include subjective statements only when the speaker explicitly states them in the message; preserve their meaning without adding interpretation.
Stop once every explicit distinct claim has its own candidate; do not infer unstated facts or expand beyond the message.

solves: General failure mechanism: extraction creates one summary candidate per message, dropping explicitly stated subjective/affective claims, so later questions about feelings cannot be answered. Applies to future sessions where a single message contains both a factual event and an explicit subjective reaction or evaluation; the skill splits them into separate candidates. Does not apply when a message contains only one claim or when the feeling is implied rather than explicitly stated.
